Subject: Tier move + feature consolidation questions

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier this week — Tom and I dug into our Q2 usage and we have a few concrete questions as we consider moving some services off our current Mid tier into a higher-throughput pool. I attached our usage extract (Straddle_Usage_Report_Q2.csv).

High-level asks:
- Can you outline pros/cons for a straight tier upgrade vs. a hybrid (keep some features on Mid, move inference-heavy routes to Throughput)?
- Any recommended feature-bundling approaches to avoid regressions when we consolidate entitlements?
- What discount/commit thresholds would apply if we committed to a 12-month Dedicated capacity window for steady traffic?

Our main concerns are: migration disruption, preserving latency SLAs for the routing-heavy endpoints, and not overpaying for features we won't use. We can do a 30–45 minute call next week to walk through the usage and your recommendations.

Appreciate the help — attached the CSV and a short internal note.

Best,
Sara Lin
Head of Partnerships, Straddle Health
(415) 555-0192

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Tier move + feature consolidation questions

Hi Sara — thanks for the data and context. I reviewed the CSV quickly and have a proposed framework below; happy to walk through on a call and tailor the numbers.

Short takeaway: a hybrid approach usually gives the best cost/latency balance for customers with spiky reranking/generation routes. Move the top 20% token-volume routes to Throughput (reserved) and leave interactive admin/low-volume actions on Mid.

Suggested framework (high level):
- Migration phasing: 2–3 week pilot (10% traffic to Throughput, end-to-end latency tests), 4 week ramp to 50%, then full shift if SLOs met.
- Feature stitching: create a single entitlement bundle for inference-heavy flows (Model Rerank + Streaming) and keep non-critical features decoupled (Analytics, Export). That minimizes entitlement churn during rollouts.
- Discounts/commits: standard committed corridor gives 8-12% discount at $75k+/month committed spend; add-on reserved GPU credits can reduce unit cost further. For a 12-month Dedicated commit we can discuss a stepped discount (10% at T1, 12% at T2) depending on sustained throughput.

I'll loop in Ben and Kim to confirm the exact concession bands and SLA implications. If you're available Tue or Wed afternoon PT, I'll schedule 30 minutes and bring a migration checklist.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick sync to align on goal metrics (latency p95, token budget)
2) We run a pilot config and share telemetry for 2 weeks
3) Draft amendment with commit/discount options for approval

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Subject: Straddle Health — Proposed upgrade path and consolidation plan

Hi Sara — thank you again for the data and the concise goals. Per our internal review (Ben/Kim included), please find the recommended path below and the next steps to move forward. I attached the draft amendment (Proposed_Amendment_v2.docx) with the exact pricing bands.

Executive summary:
- Recommended approach: Hybrid throughput model. Move inference-heavy routes (approx. 18–22% of token volume) to a Dedicated throughput pool and keep control-plane features on Mid tier. This minimizes latency risk and reduces monthly token spend by ~12% compared to a full upgrade.
- Discounts & credits offered: 12-month Dedicated commit with 10% off unit rates + one-time migration credit equal to 3 months of committed spend (applied as invoice credit). We can structure a mid-contract review at 6 months to validate usage and adjust reserved credit sizes.
- Feature bundling: we will create a separate entitlements bundle for High-Throughput endpoints (Rerank + Streaming + KV cache) and export Analytics as an optional add-on. That keeps your ability to toggle features during ramp.

Attachments: Proposed_Amendment_v2.docx, Straddle_Usage_Report_Q2.csv (you previously shared).
Actionable next steps:
1) Review the draft amendment and call out any edits by EOD Fri PT (I'll collect edits and send a final DocuSign link).
2) Approve pilot start date — we suggest Nov 1 as a pilot kickoff (2 weeks).
3) Kick off a short architecture call with our Ops lead to map routing rules and fallback policy.

Doc link: https://hubspot.com/deals/STRD-482 (proposal and redlines), Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bStraddlePlan

If that sounds good I can send the DocuSign for the amendment and schedule the pilot planning call.

Best,
